goals: Ask for things and report progress at work
Give reasons, add points and disagree politely

lessons.title: Asking a colleague for something
lessons.learn: Workplace requests are short and polite: ज़रा यह भेज दीजिए (please send this), क्या आप मुझे फ़ाइल दे सकते हैं? (could you give me the file?), मुझे इसकी ज़रूरत है (I need this). The compound भेज दीजिए is why the tone works: देना alone is flat, देना with दीजिए hands the result over.

grammar.title: क्या आप … सकते हैं? · ज़रा … दीजिए
grammar.explain: क्या आप + verb stem + सकते हैं? is the standard 'could you': क्या आप यह भेज सकते हैं? Its informal twin is ज़रा … दीजिए. मुझे इसकी ज़रूरत है states the need without asking, which colleagues read as a request and learners often miss.
grammar.pattern: क्या आप … सकते हैं? · ज़रा … दीजिए · मुझे इसकी ज़रूरत है

examples.t: क्या आप मुझे फ़ाइल भेज सकते हैं?
examples.r: kyā āp mujhe fāil bhej sakte haiṅ?
examples.en: Could you send me the file?

examples.t: ज़रा यह ईमेल भेज दीजिए।
examples.r: zarā yah īmel bhej dījie.
examples.en: Please send this email over.

examples.t: मुझे इसकी ज़रूरत है — आज शाम तक।
examples.r: mujhe iskī zarūrat hai — āj śām tak.
examples.en: I need this — by this evening.

mistakes.wrong: आप यह भेजो। (to a colleague at work)
mistakes.right: क्या आप यह भेज दीजिए? / ज़रा यह भेज दीजिए।
mistakes.why: भेजो is तुम-form and behaves like an instruction. At work, even with a peer, the request shape is the norm — the difference is not hierarchy but register.

dialogue.t: क्या आप मुझे पिछला फ़ाइल भेज सकते हैं?
dialogue.r: kyā āp mujhe pichhlā fāil bhej sakte haiṅ?
dialogue.en: Could you send me the previous file?

dialogue.t: ज़रूर — अभी भेज देती हूँ।
dialogue.r: zarūr — abhī bhej detī hūṅ.
dialogue.en: Certainly — I am sending it now.

dialogue.t: धन्यवाद। इसकी ज़रूरत आज शाम तक है।
dialogue.r: dhanyavād. iskī zarūrat āj śām tak hai.
dialogue.en: Thank you. I need it by this evening.

dialogue.t: समझ गई। कुछ और चाहिए तो बताइए।
dialogue.r: samajh gaī. kuchh aur cāhie to batāie.
dialogue.en: Understood. If you need anything else, tell me.

lessons.title: Explaining a delay
lessons.learn: In a workplace, a delay is explained with देर हो गई (it got late) rather than a blame sentence, plus a reason and a new deadline: देर हो गई क्योंकि फ़ाइल नहीं मिली — कल शाम तक पूरा कर दूँगा. ठीक हो गया काम की वजह से (because of work) uses की वजह से, the standard 'because of'.

grammar.title: देर हो गई, क्योंकि … — कल तक कर दूँगा
grammar.explain: The delay is stated as an event with no agent (देर हो गई), the reason is attached with क्योंकि or की वजह से, and the repair is a specific new commitment (कल शाम तक कर दूँगा). Ending with माफ़ी in front — माफ़ी, देर हो गई — is the normal opening of the whole move.
grammar.pattern: माफ़ी, देर हो गई क्योंकि … · … तक कर दूँगा

examples.t: माफ़ी, देर हो गई क्योंकि फ़ाइल नहीं मिली।
examples.r: māfī, der ho gaī kyoṅki fāil nahīṅ milī.
examples.en: Sorry, it got late because I could not find the file.

examples.t: ट्रैफ़िक की वजह से देर हो गई।
examples.r: ṭraifik kī vajah se der ho gaī.
examples.en: It got late because of the traffic.

examples.t: कोशिश करूँगा — कल शाम तक पूरा कर दूँगा।
examples.r: kośiś karūṅgā — kal śām tak pūrā kar dūṅgā.
examples.en: I will try — I will finish it by tomorrow evening.

mistakes.why: मैंने देर की names you as the cause and sounds like a confession. देर हो गई reports the delay as something that happened — which is why it is the workplace form.

dialogue.t: रिपोर्ट कहाँ है? कल चाहिए थी।
dialogue.r: riporṭ kahāṅ hai? kal cāhie thī.
dialogue.en: Where is the report? It was needed yesterday.

dialogue.t: माफ़ी, देर हो गई क्योंकि आँकड़े अधूरे थे।
dialogue.r: māfī, der ho gaī kyoṅki āṅkṛe adhūre the.
dialogue.en: Sorry, it got late because the figures were incomplete.

dialogue.t: तो अब कब तक?
dialogue.r: to ab kab tak?
dialogue.en: So by when now?

dialogue.t: कल शाम तक पूरा कर दूँगा — कोशिश करूँगा, आज भी भेज दूँ।
dialogue.r: kal śām tak pūrā kar dūṅgā — kośiś karūṅgā, āj bhī bhej dūṅ.
dialogue.en: I will finish it by tomorrow evening — I will try to send it today as well.

lessons.title: Email and message register
lessons.learn: Written workplace Hindi opens with नमस्ते or प्रिय (dear) and closes with धन्यवाद and सादर (respectfully). The body uses सूचित करना (to inform), कृपया (please), and भेज रहा हूँ (I am sending). प्रिय is for letters and formal email; नमस्ते works for both and is safer.

grammar.title: Opening, body verbs, closing
grammar.explain: Hindi email has three fixed zones. Opening: नमस्ते / प्रिय. Body: सूचित करना (inform), कृपया … (please), संलग्न है (is attached), प्रतिक्रिया दीजिए (give feedback). Closing: धन्यवाद / सादर. The body prefers the passive-ish impersonal: संलग्न फ़ाइल कृपया देख लीजिए.
grammar.pattern: नमस्ते → सूचित करता हूँ कि … → कृपया … → धन्यवाद/सादर

examples.t: नमस्ते, सूचित कर रहा हूँ कि फ़ाइल संलग्न है।
examples.r: namaste, sūcit kar rahā hūṅ ki fāil saṅlagn hai.
examples.en: Hello, I am informing you that the file is attached.

examples.t: कृपया इसे जाँच लीजिए।
examples.r: kṛpayā ise jāṅc lījie.
examples.en: Please check this.

examples.t: धन्यवाद। सादर।
examples.r: dhanyavād. sādar.
examples.en: Thank you. Respectfully.

mistakes.wrong: मैं आपको बताता हूँ कि फ़ाइल भेज दिया।
mistakes.right: सूचित करता हूँ कि फ़ाइल भेज दी गई है।
mistakes.why: बताना is conversational; written workplace Hindi uses सूचित करना. And a sent file is reported as भेज दी गई है — the thing, not the person, carries the verb.

dialogue.en: I am informing you that the attached file is final. Please check it and give feedback. Thank you — respectfully.

lessons.title: Reasons: क्योंकि, इसलिए, इसका मतलब है कि
lessons.learn: क्योंकि gives the reason after the fact, इसलिए gives the result after the reason, and इसका मतलब है कि draws the inference. Only one of क्योंकि/इसलिए belongs in a sentence pair — using both is the commonest B1 slip: क्योंकि बारिश हुई, इसलिए हम रुके (not क्योंकि… इसलिए… in the same clause).

grammar.title: One reason, one result
grammar.explain: क्योंकि … इसलिए never pair inside one bound sentence: either बारिश हुई, इसलिए हम रुके, or हम रुके क्योंकि बारिश हुई. In writing they can meet only across two full sentences. इसका मतलब है कि introduces what follows from what was just said, and it is the workhorse of an argument.
grammar.pattern: … इसलिए … · … क्योंकि … · इसका मतलब है कि …

examples.t: बारिश हुई, इसलिए हम रुके।
examples.r: bāriś huī, islie ham ruke.
examples.en: It rained, so we stopped.

examples.t: हम रुके क्योंकि बारिश हो रही थी।
examples.r: ham ruke kyoṅki bāriś ho rahī thī.
examples.en: We stopped because it was raining.

examples.t: इसका मतलब है कि योजना बदलनी पड़ेगी।
examples.r: iskā matlab hai ki yojnā badalnī paṛegī.
examples.en: This means the plan will have to change.

mistakes.wrong: क्योंकि बारिश हुई, इसलिए हम रुके।
mistakes.right: बारिश हुई, इसलिए हम रुके। / हम रुके क्योंकि बारिश हुई।
mistakes.why: क्योंकि and इसलिए each carry the same link from opposite ends. Keeping both in one sentence is the English 'because … so' pattern, which Hindi does not use.

lessons.title: Adding and contrasting: इसके अलावा, हालाँकि
lessons.learn: इसके अलावा (besides this) adds a point in the same direction; दूसरी ओर (on the other hand) and हालाँकि (although) turn. The order matters: Hindi builds the case first and turns late, and a turn that arrives in the first sentence reads as a refusal to discuss.

grammar.title: Add, then turn
grammar.explain: इसके अलावा and और भी extend the argument; हालाँकि is a written 'although' that opens a clause, and दूसरी ओर balances two sides. लेकिन joins inside a sentence. The pattern in a paragraph: claim, इसके अलावा, लेकिन/हालाँकि — the turn is last because the reader needs the case in hand before it turns.
grammar.pattern: … इसके अलावा … · हालाँकि …, फिर भी … · दूसरी ओर …

mistakes.why: हालाँकि leads with the concession and फिर भी carries the turn. Reversing them makes the sentence disagree before it has heard the point.

lessons.title: Disagreeing without a fight
lessons.learn: The polite disagreement concedes a piece, names the gap, and proposes: आपकी बात सही है, पर एक बात रह गई (your point is right, but one thing was missed). मुझे लगता है (it seems to me) softens everything after it, and थोड़ी आपत्ति है (I have a small objection) is how a formal objection opens.

grammar.title: Concede, name the gap, propose
grammar.explain: Three beats: आपकी बात सही है (concede), पर एक बात रह गई / मुझे लगता है कि (gap), तो हम … कर सकते हैं? (propose). मुझे लगता है takes the को-form and can carry a whole objection politely — मुझे लगता है कि यह समय कम है.
grammar.pattern: आपकी बात सही है, पर … · मुझे लगता है कि … · तो हम … कर सकते हैं?

lessons.title: Forms and offices: आवेदन, प्रमाण, हस्ताक्षर
lessons.learn: A form in Hindi asks for the same few things in a fixed order: नाम, पिता का नाम, पता, तारीख़, हस्ताक्षर. What you submit is an आवेदन (application), what proves something is a प्रमाण (certificate), and what you keep is a प्रतिलिपि (copy). Learning these five words removes most of the fear of an Indian office.

grammar.title: जमा करना · के लिए · कहाँ मिलेगा?
grammar.explain: Applications are जमा करना (submitted) at a desk, and के लिए marks what they are for: वीज़ा के लिए आवेदन. To find the right window: प्रमाण पत्र कहाँ मिलेगा? and to check requirements: क्या चाहिए? — क्या मूल प्रमाण चाहिए या प्रतिलिपि?
grammar.pattern: … के लिए आवेदन · … जमा करना · कहाँ मिलेगा?

lessons.title: Official verbs: सूचित, निवेदन, अनुरोध
lessons.learn: Three verbs run institutional Hindi: सूचित करना (to inform), निवेदन करना (to request, formal and slightly supplicating), अनुरोध करना (to request, neutral). They are used impersonally — सूचित किया जाता है (it is informed), निवेदन है कि … (it is requested that …) — which is exactly why a letter looks unlike speech.

grammar.title: Impersonal institutional verbs
grammar.explain: Institutional writing prefers the impersonal: सूचित किया जाता है, निवेदन है कि, आदेश दिया गया है. The passive जाना-form removes the person, which is the point — a notice is not about who wrote it. In speech the same content uses बताया and कहा; the switch is register, not grammar.

lessons.title: Asking for clarification
lessons.learn: The most valuable institutional sentence is मैं समझा नहीं, ज़रा दोबारा बताइए (I did not understand, please tell me again). Then: कृपया स्पष्ट कीजिए (please clarify), इसका मतलब क्या है? (what does this mean?), लिखकर दे दीजिए (give it in writing). Nobody minds being asked twice; everybody minds being misunderstood.

grammar.title: मैं समझा नहीं · कृपया स्पष्ट कीजिए
grammar.explain: समझा नहीं is the fixed shape of 'I did not get it' — masculine agreement for a male speaker, समझी नहीं for a female speaker. कृपया स्पष्ट कीजिए is the polite request for a clarification, and लिखकर दीजिए asks for it in writing, which in a government office is a completely normal request.
grammar.pattern: मैं समझा/समझी नहीं · कृपया स्पष्ट कीजिए · लिखकर दे दीजिए

culture.text: Hinglish — Hindi and English mixed inside a sentence — is the ordinary register of Indian offices, and treating it as bad Hindi misunderstands how it works. The mixing follows rules: English supplies nouns and technical terms (file, meeting, deadline, report), Hindi supplies the grammar that carries them (भेज दीजिए, हो गया, कर लीजिए). A learner who can say फ़ाइल भेज दीजिए sounds more fluent to a colleague than one who builds a pure-Hindi sentence nobody in that office has ever spoken — and the same learner still needs the formal register for anything written.

reading.text: पिछले हफ़्ते दफ़्तर में एक बैठक हुई। विषय था: नई प्रक्रिया। पहले प्रबंधक ने बताया कि फ़ॉर्म बदल गया है। इसके अलावा, अब हस्ताक्षर के साथ तारीख़ भी ज़रूरी है। कुछ लोगों ने आपत्ति की — पुरानी प्रक्रिया आसान थी। हालाँकि उनकी बात सही थी, फिर भी बदलाव ज़रूरी था। आख़िर में तय हुआ कि नई प्रक्रिया अगले सोमवार से लागू होगी, और सबको लिखकर सूचित किया जाएगा। मैंने भी एक सुझाव रखा: एक हफ़्ते का समय दिया जाए। मान लिया गया।
reading.gloss: Last week there was a meeting at the office. The subject was: the new procedure. First the manager said that the form has changed. Besides that, a date is now needed along with the signature. Some people objected — the old procedure was easier. Although their point was right, the change was still necessary. Finally it was decided that the new procedure would apply from next Monday, and everyone would be informed in writing. I also put forward a suggestion: that a week's time be given. It was accepted.

mistakes.why: मदद is a noun, and helping someone is उसकी मदद करना — the helper is the owner. मदद किया treats it like a verb and is heard immediately.

mistakes.wrong: बैठक में मैंने कहा कि मुझे देर होगी। (reporting a past statement)
mistakes.right: बैठक में मैंने कहा कि मुझे देर होगी। / … हो जाएगी।
mistakes.why: Hindi keeps the tense of reported speech, so होगी stays futuristic inside a past sentence. Learners shift it to past because English would — and the sentence then claims a delay that has already been decided differently.
कृपया plus आप doubles the politeness and reads as stiff, and thisको/उसको is conversational where इसे is the written form. Institutional Hindi trims rather than layers.

task.title: Write a workplace message twice
task.instructions: Write the same message two ways: once as a WhatsApp note to a colleague, once as an email to a manager. Same request, same deadline. Then underline every place the two versions differ — the pronouns, the verbs, the closing. The difference between the two versions is the register, and learning to see it is the point of this rung.
